compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

`transition_ticket(fattish-plucky-bufflehead, "in_progress" -> "closed")` over MCP
returned `McpError: -32001: Request timed out` on three successive attempts. The
ticket stayed `in_progress` each time. The call runs the completion-verifier close
gate inline, and that gate takes 9-11 minutes by `AGENTS.md`'s own published
estimate, against an MCP client request deadline of roughly 60 seconds.

The timeout is not a verdict. The server keeps running, the caller learns nothing,
and the natural response is to re-fire the same call -- a second billable gate pass.
This is precisely the failure `AGENTS.md` already describes for the direct gate
tools, and the reason `review_plan_start` / `verify_completion_start` exist.

## Why the existing workaround does not cover it

Pre-computing the attestation does NOT make the close fast. Measured on
`62dc-535b-5d05-421d` at `origin/main` `f1fe7c6f587d3a57fcd4b49598485d7fd4101711`:

1. `verify_completion_start` -> job
   `1793725995508270393-89be127e921a4bf8b7acd1bbfaee7749`.
2. `gate_status` -> `status: "passed"`, `verdict: "PASS"`,
   `verified_at_sha: f1fe7c6f587...`, `signed_at: 1793726842234944794`.
3. `transition_ticket` with that signed certificate in place -> **timed out again**.

So the async surface covers the gate op but not the operation that actually needs
it. An agent that follows the documented guidance still cannot close a ticket over
MCP without an ambiguous timeout.

## Scope: which surfaces run a gate with no async counterpart

In `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, `_start_gate_job` (:213-258) and `_spawn_gate_daemon`
(:174-210) are already generic over `gate_type` -- the daemon machinery is not
specific to the two gates that use it. But:

- `_register_gate_start_tools` (:261-342) registers exactly two starters:
  `review_plan_start` (:265) and `verify_completion_start` (:304).
- `_gate_sidecar_fields` (:162-171) hard-restricts to
  `{"plan_review", "verify_completion"}`.

Surfaces that run one of these gates inline and have NO async form:

| Surface | Gate run inline | Async form |
|---|---|---|
| `transition_ticket` (`_mcp_tool_specs.py:649`) | completion-verifier on close; plan-review on claim-equivalent transitions (:657) | none |
| `claim_ticket` (`_mcp_tool_specs.py:217`) | plan-review | none |
| `review_code` (`_mcp_llm.py:354`) | code review | none |

`review_code` is the clearest gap of the three: it is a long LLM gate op registered
synchronously alongside `review_plan` and `verify_completion`, which both got
starters, and it was simply not given one.

## The invariant to establish

Every MCP surface that can run the plan-review, completion-verifier, or code-review
gate must have an async counterpart returning a `{job_id, ..., status: "running"}`
handle pollable by `gate_status`, so no caller is ever forced into a request that
can outlive the client deadline. Today that invariant holds for 2 surfaces and
fails for 3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 -- `review_code_start` exists, returns a `{job_id, ticket_id, gate_type,
      status: "running"}` handle in milliseconds, and its job is pollable through
      `gate_status` to a terminal `passed`/`failed` with the review result.
- [ ] AC2 -- `claim_ticket` and `transition_ticket` each have an async counterpart
      (or an async mode) that starts the gate on the daemon, returns a handle
      immediately, and applies the status change on gate success -- so the
      state transition itself is never blocked on an inline gate run.
- [ ] AC3 -- `gate_status` reports the new gate types, and `_gate_sidecar_fields`
      no longer silently drops sidecar provenance for them.
- [ ] AC4 -- a test drives each new starter through `gate_status` to a terminal
      state, asserting the handle is returned before the gate completes (the
      point of the change is the immediate return, so a test that only checks the
      terminal verdict does not cover it).
- [ ] AC5 -- a test asserts the invariant directly: every registered MCP tool that
      can run one of the three gates has an async counterpart. This is the
      regression guard that stops a fourth surface shipping without one.
- [ ] AC6 -- `docs/mcp-reference.md` documents the new starters, and the
      `AGENTS.md` guidance that currently names only `review_plan` /
      `verify_completion` is widened to cover every gate-running surface.
- [ ] AC7 -- de-dup protection applies to the new surfaces as it does to the
      synchronous `review_plan` / `verify_completion`, so a re-fire after a
      timeout attaches to the in-flight run instead of double-billing.

## Provider neutrality

Nothing here is provider- or model-specific. The daemon machinery, the job handle,
and the polling surface are all transport-level; they are indifferent to which
provider backs the gate.

## Out of scope

- Changing any gate's verdict logic, prompt, or criteria.
- Raising the MCP client request deadline -- that is a client setting and would not
  fix a 10-minute gate behind a 60-second deadline anyway.
- The CLI surfaces, which are not subject to the MCP request deadline.
compiled_state.title: Gate-running MCP surfaces lack async counterparts, so closes time out
